item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ Crit
- lots of spag issues

Large portions of the East-coast of the US are obliterated.

East coast in this usage is not hyphenated, and both words should be capitalized.

North & South Carolina as well as Florida destroyed and replaced by an enormous crater.

This is a weird way to list the states. "North Carolina, South Carolina and Florida" would be the most clinical.

Foundation enacts the ARC protocol, evacuating selected beings for transport off Earth for humanity's survival.

The sense of enact is wrong here, as they only begin the protocol at this moment. Additionally, Protocol would likely be capitalized as well.

E-42/06-9 makes contact with the US again, this time appearing to destroy North Dakota, Montana and Minnesota and heaping up the earth's crust toward itself

If it's only appearing to destroy those states, what's actually happening? "this time destroying North Dakota".

Only 4 of 20 ARK Spacecraft survive the second assault and are immediately launched into space.

Technically, both of these numbers should be spelled, but this can pass for the joke. However, ARC is spelled with a K here.

04-1-2019//15h50: Countdown begins for ARC Spacecraft to use Experimental "Sugiyati FTL-Drive". Hoping to accelerate themselves out of immediate danger.

Replace the period with a comma, the second sentence is not an independent clause.

04-1-2019//16h22: All contact with Earth Lost.

Lost should not be capitalized.

The Earth's mantle begins extruding from the massive crater off the east-coast.

Previous issues with East Coast still apply, and you should specify the East Coast of what exactly. While the United States has previously been stated, this is a global event and there are many east coasts. This could be anywhere.

We may number in the thousands but we carry the hopes and dreams of the millions we left behind

Billions is more appropriate here.

That being said, The image we captured before leaving earth will be buried under Level 6 ARK Command Security

The should not be capitalized. Additionally, it's spelled with an K here again, where it's otherwise a C.
